chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I had a friend from the scribes of the Banu Umayya who said to me, 'Ask permission for me to see Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).' So I asked permission for him, and he granted it. When he entered, he offered greetings and sat down, then spoke a few words: 'I am your ransom, I used to write in the diwan (office) of these people, and I acquired from their worldly wealth a great deal, and I kept it hidden (did not spend it).'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Had it not been for the Banu Umayya finding someone to write for them, collect the booty (fay') for them, fight on their behalf, and witness their community, they would not have deprived us of our right. And if people left them and what was in their hands, they would not find anything except what fell into their own hands.'

The young man said, 'I am your ransom, is there an exit for me from it?' He said, 'If I tell you to do something, will you do it?' He said, 'I will.' He said, 'Then withdraw from all that you acquired from their diwan. Whoever you know among them, return his wealth to him, and whoever you do not know, give charity on his behalf. And I guarantee for you, by Allah, the Paradise.'
The young man pondered for a long time, then said to him, 'I have done it, I am your ransom.'

Ibn Abi Hamzah said: The young man returned with us to Kufa, and he did not leave anything on the face of the earth except that it came out from him, even the clothes on his body. We divided a portion for him, bought him clothes, and sent him provisions.
Not many months passed until he fell ill, and we used to visit him.
One day I entered while he was in the process of dying (sawq), so he opened his eyes and said to me, 'O Ali, your companion has fulfilled his promise, by Allah.'

Then he died, and we took care of his affairs. I went out until I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). When he looked at me, he said, 'O Ali, we have fulfilled (our guarantee) for your companion, by Allah.'
I said, 'You are truthful, I am your ransom.' He said to me, 'This is how it was, by Allah, when he died.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wealth acquired from unjust rulers and how does one purify it according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the concept of *khumus* (one-fifth tax) and the purification of wealth acquired from unjust rulers, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding *ghulul* (plunder). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes that the Umayyads' hold on power relied on the administrative and military support of the people, and their wealth was essentially a loan from the public treasury. The narrative highlights the spiritual weight of returning usurped rights, with the Imam’s personal guarantee of Paradise underscoring the high status of this act of restitution.
